text: Which of the following is/are a tautology? (a) (a or b) -> (b and c)  (b) (a and b) -> (b or c)  (c) (a or b) -> (b -> c)  (d) a -> b -> (b -> c)
solution: (a∧b)→(b∨c) ≡ ¬(a∧b)∨b∨c ≡ ¬a∨¬b∨b∨c ≡ T. (A) fails when c=F; (C) fails when b=T, c=F; (D), read right-associatively, fails when a=T, b=T, c=F. Option (d) is read right-associatively, a -> (b -> (b -> c)); under a left-associative reading it would be ((a -> b) -> (b -> c)), which is also not a tautology, so the answer does not depend on the convention.
